title: spec-gate v0: the first trusted judge
description:
## Goal

`spec-gate` v0: the first trusted judge. It runs `spec-gate-specs` against a `spec-gate` commit and refuses a scenario that was never seen red. It fails a run on skipped or undefined steps, and on zero scenarios. It mints scenario ids. It refuses to run when its own checksum differs from the pin. Everything else in `docs/design.md` is out of v0.

## In scope (criteria in `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md`)

- `sg-dop.1`, `sg-dop.2`: the verdict names the product and spec commits, and the spec version is chosen by the spec repository.
- `sg-397.1`–`.3`: red-first.
- `sg-zf8.1`, `sg-zf8.2`: an undefined step or zero scenarios fails the run.
- `sg-i86.1`: checksum refusal.
- The scenario-id minting criteria drafted in `gate-c7r.1`.

## Out of scope

- `sg-3zr.*`: the binding check, owned by `binding-contract` (D-24).
- `sg-ubq.*`: local vs authoritative runs, which need the runner (D-16).
- `sg-212.1`: the full agent report.
- The holdout, mutation-through-specs, structure, purity and contract stages; the runner host; commit statuses; the `rule-gate` write block (D-22). In v0, the separation between the spec and product repositories is held by operator review alone.

## How the bootstrap works

1. The product scaffold commit builds a stub binary that implements no behaviour. It is the red baseline: every in-scope scenario fails against it for its stated reason.
2. v0 is built and reviewed, tagged `v0`, and its checksum is pinned.
3. Pinned v0 mints `@id` tags into `spec-gate-specs` (reviewed and merged by the operator).
4. Pinned v0 judges the scaffold commit, which records the reds in the ledger.
5. Pinned v0 judges the `v0` commit, which records the greens.

The only self-judgment is step 5. D-19 accepts it: v0 is trusted on review. From the next release on, a judge is always certified by its predecessor (D-18).

## Known limits of v0

- A scenario whose first recorded result is a pass stays rejected under its id. The way out is to remove the `@id` tag and re-mint, which gives a new identity (see `gate-c7r.7`).
- A scenario whose text changes after it was counted keeps its red-first evidence. Nothing in v0 detects that the meaning changed.

## Success Criteria

- Every in-scope scenario has a ledger red against the scaffold commit, and a later green against the `v0` commit.
- The acceptance harness was seen failing on a deliberately undefined step.
- The operator has reviewed v0, signed tag `v0`, and pinned its sha256 in `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.toml`.
- The ledger and the `@id` tags are merged to `spec-gate-specs` `main`.

## Operator decision

> "accept all" — operator, 2026-10-21, accepting the recommendations for D-01 to D-25 as recorded in `docs/design.md` §10.

> "commit both and file the v0 epic" — operator, 2026-10-21.

> "find a way to make it work" — operator, 2026-10-21, in reply to the two flagged assumptions: whether mint is in v0, and how seed reds are recorded before v0 exists.

Approves:

- The 25 decisions as worded in `docs/design.md` §10.
- Filing this epic.
- `spec-gate mint` as part of v0. Red-first keys its ledger on minted ids (D-20), and ids are never written by hand, so v0 has no red-first without mint.
- The bootstrap above. The scaffold commit is the red baseline, and pinned v0 records reds and greens itself, so no ledger entry is written by hand.
- Replacing the `[gates] acceptance` entry's `suite` key in `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.toml` with the harness-command contract from `gate-c7r.5`, and updating `docs/design.md` §6 and §7 to match. This is what makes fixture spec repositories cheap to run inside the acceptance harness.
- The gates that house rules require in the two new repositories: `hex-lint` roles (cm-hkg), `effect-audit`, `clippy::wildcard_enum_match_arm` at deny (cm-prk), a no-comments gate (cm-k7c), nextest (cm-wah), `hegeltest` (cm-eqj), and `cargo mutants` with `mutation-triage` (cm-1qk).

Nothing else is approved:

- no edits to `~/code/tools` or `~/kbe`;
- no changes to existing requirements or scenarios except agent drafts merged by the operator (D-15);
- no scope beyond the in-scope list above.

title: Draft the scenario-id minting requirement and scenarios in spec-gate-specs
description:
## Context (applies to every bead in epic gate-c7r)

`spec-gate` runs a product's executable specification from a separate spec repository and gates the product on the verdict. Invariant: the agent that changes the product may not touch the measurement (specs, drivers, ledger, judge pin, verdict). Two repositories:

- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate`: the product (the tool). Agents write here.
- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate-specs`: its spec repository. Agents only draft here, on a branch the operator merges (D-09, D-15). The agent that changes one repository in a task does not change the other in that task (D-11).

`spec-gate` is the first product judged by `spec-gate` (dog-fooding). Design and the 25 recorded decisions: `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate/docs/design.md`. Requirements: `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md` (ids minted by `~/code/tools/req`, never by hand). House rules: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (rule ids `cm-*`).

## What

Draft, in `spec-gate-specs`, the requirement and scenarios for scenario-id minting (D-20). `spec-gate mint`:
- gives every scenario that lacks one an `@id:<hashid>` tag;
- never overwrites an existing id;
- never reuses an id, including the id of a deleted scenario;
- decides uniqueness against every feature file in the repository, never against a narrowed subset.

Also draft the consequence for judging: a scenario without an `@id` cannot be recorded in the ledger, so `spec-gate judge` fails the judgment, naming the scenario.

Follow `req`'s minting rules (`~/code/tools/req/SPEC.md`, the "IDS" section) and the house spec style (`~/kbe/guides/writing-specifications.md`): an EARS clause, a witness and a near-miss for each requirement, and the zero, one and many cases (cm-srn).

This is a spec-repository draft. It reaches `main` only by operator merge (D-15).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The requirement is in `spec-gate.req.md`, with ids minted by `req mint`, and `req check --out requirements.toon` is clean.
- Each new criterion has exactly one scenario tagged `@covers:<criterion-id>`.
- One scenario covers judging a scenario that has no `@id`.
- The scenarios cover zero, one and many untagged scenarios; an already-tagged scenario left unchanged; and a second run that changes nothing.
- Delivered as a branch on `spec-gate-specs`; nothing reaches `main` without operator merge.

title: spec-gate judge
description:
## Context (applies to every bead in epic gate-c7r)

`spec-gate` runs a product's executable specification from a separate spec repository and gates the product on the verdict. Invariant: the agent that changes the product may not touch the measurement (specs, drivers, ledger, judge pin, verdict). Two repositories:

- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate`: the product (the tool). Agents write here.
- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate-specs`: its spec repository. Agents only draft here, on a branch the operator merges (D-09, D-15). The agent that changes one repository in a task does not change the other in that task (D-11).

`spec-gate` is the first product judged by `spec-gate` (dog-fooding). Design and the 25 recorded decisions: `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate/docs/design.md`. Requirements: `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md` (ids minted by `~/code/tools/req`, never by hand). House rules: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (rule ids `cm-*`).

## What

The `spec-gate judge` use case: one authoritative judgment of a product commit.

- **Spec commit.** Take it from the spec repository's `main` commit. A spec checkout that is dirty or not on `main` gives a void verdict naming the cause. Anything the product commit says about spec versions is ignored (`sg-dop.2`).
- **Product.** Check out the product commit and build it per `[sut]`. A build failure is void, not fail.
- **Harness.** Run the acceptance command from `[gates] acceptance` and read its results file in the contract format. A missing or malformed results file is void.
- **Core.** Hand the results and the ledger to the core (`gate-c7r.7`).
- **Ledger.** Append one entry per scenario.
- **Output.** Write the verdict document naming both commits (`sg-dop.1`) and exit with the contract status.

Effects sit behind ports: git, build, harness runner, ledger store, verdict sink. The use case itself holds no I/O.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests against fake adapters at every port (cm-wah) cover pass, fail, and each void cause: dirty spec checkout, spec checkout not on `main`, build failure, harness failure, missing results, malformed results.
- Ledger appends are proven append-only: a test checks that the earlier bytes are unchanged after a judgment.
- A few boundary integration tests with real git repositories in a temporary directory (cm-33k).
- `cargo mutants` on the changed code, with survivors triaged.
- The `sg-dop.*`, `sg-397.*` and `sg-zf8.*` scenarios pass when the harness runs against this commit.

title: Checksum refusal
description:
## Context (applies to every bead in epic gate-c7r)

- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate`: the product (the tool). Agents write here.
- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate-specs`: its spec repository. Agents only draft here, on a branch the operator merges (D-09, D-15). The agent that changes one repository in a task does not change the other in that task (D-11).

`spec-gate` is the first product judged by `spec-gate` (dog-fooding). Design and the 25 recorded decisions: `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate/docs/design.md`. Requirements: `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md` (ids minted by `~/code/tools/req`, never by hand). House rules: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (rule ids `cm-*`).

## What

The checksum refusal (`sg-i86.1`). Before any other action, `spec-gate judge` computes the checksum of its own running binary and compares it with `[judge] sha256` in the spec repository's `spec-gate.toml`. On a mismatch, it refuses with the contract's refused status and names both checksums. A missing or `PENDING` pin also refuses, naming the cause. The judge is never the commit under test (D-18).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests against a fake binary-identity port cover: match, mismatch, missing pin, and `PENDING` pin.
- One boundary integration test runs the real binary against a pin it cannot match.
- `cargo mutants` on the changed code, with survivors triaged.
- The `sg-i86.1` scenario passes when the harness runs against this commit.

title: Spec workspace: DSL, driver port, CLI driver with fixtures and lying-fake self-test
description:
## Context (applies to every bead in epic gate-c7r)

`spec-gate` runs a product's executable specification from a separate spec repository and gates the product on the verdict. Invariant: the agent that changes the product may not touch the measurement (specs, drivers, ledger, judge pin, verdict). Two repositories:

- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate`: the product (the tool). Agents write here.
- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate-specs`: its spec repository. Agents only draft here, on a branch the operator merges (D-09, D-15). The agent that changes one repository in a task does not change the other in that task (D-11).

`spec-gate` is the first product judged by `spec-gate` (dog-fooding). Design and the 25 recorded decisions: `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate/docs/design.md`. Requirements: `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md` (ids minted by `~/code/tools/req`, never by hand). House rules: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (rule ids `cm-*`).

## What

The spec workspace in `spec-gate-specs` that drives the `spec-gate` binary as a black box. Its layering is described in `docs/design.md` §3.

- **Crates:**
  - `dsl`: domain operations in spec-gate's own vocabulary, with aliasing so scenarios run in parallel (D-02, D-03);
  - `driver-port`;
  - `driver-cli`;
  - `acceptance`: the `cucumber` 0.23 harness (D-01, D-23).
  
  `dsl` depends on no `spec-gate` crate (D-02).
- **Fixtures.** The CLI driver builds, in a temporary directory, everything a scenario needs:
  - a fixture spec repository with a ledger and a judge pin;
  - a fixture harness command that prints canned results in the format from `gate-c7r.5`;
  - a fixture product repository with commits.
  
  It observes exit status, the verdict document and ledger bytes, and never reaches into `spec-gate` internals.
- **Checksum.** Every fixture pins the checksum of the `spec-gate` binary under test, so only the checksum scenario exercises a mismatch.
- **Lying fake.** The driver carries a self-test against a fake `spec-gate` that lies (for example, it reports pass while writing no ledger entry), and the driver must detect each lie (D-11).
- **Logging.** Every driver invocation is logged per scenario: command, arguments, exit status, stdout, stderr and the fixture layout. This is the e2e debugging trail.
- **Layering gate.** `hex-lint` roles are set from the first commit. The layering `acceptance → dsl → driver-port ← driver-cli` is a build failure when broken.

This is done by an agent session that does not change `spec-gate` itself (D-11).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The lying-fake self-test was seen red against the lying fake and green against an honest fake.
- `hex-lint` passes and was seen failing on a planted forbidden edge (`dsl → driver-cli`), which was then removed.
- `cargo nextest run` passes; no test function contains a loop or branch (cm-o9o).
- Delivered as a branch on `spec-gate-specs` for operator merge.

title: Operator bootstrap: review, tag and pin v0; mint ids; record reds and greens
description:
## Context (applies to every bead in epic gate-c7r)

`spec-gate` runs a product's executable specification from a separate spec repository and gates the product on the verdict. Invariant: the agent that changes the product may not touch the measurement (specs, drivers, ledger, judge pin, verdict). Two repositories:

- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate`: the product (the tool). Agents write here.
- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate-specs`: its spec repository. Agents only draft here, on a branch the operator merges (D-09, D-15). The agent that changes one repository in a task does not change the other in that task (D-11).

`spec-gate` is the first product judged by `spec-gate` (dog-fooding). Design and the 25 recorded decisions: `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate/docs/design.md`. Requirements: `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md` (ids minted by `~/code/tools/req`, never by hand). House rules: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (rule ids `cm-*`).

## What

The operator's bootstrap of the first judge (D-19). This is not agent work. Order matters.

1. Review the v0 commit by hand.
2. Sign tag `v0`. Build it with `cargo build --release --locked` and compute its sha256.
3. Set `[judge] sha256` in `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.toml` and merge.
4. Run pinned v0's `mint` on `spec-gate-specs`. Review the diff (only `@id` tags added) and merge.
5. Run pinned v0's `judge` against the scaffold commit (SHA in `gate-c7r.8`'s close note). This records the reds.
6. Run pinned v0's `judge` against the `v0` commit. This records the greens. It is the one accepted self-judgment (D-19).
7. Commit the ledger to `spec-gate-specs` `main`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ledger holds, for every in-scope scenario, a red at the scaffold commit before a green at the `v0` commit. No ledger entry was written by hand.
- `spec-gate.toml` pins v0's sha256, and v0 refuses to run when the pin is changed by one character.
- The verdict for the `v0` commit is pass and names both commits.

title: Write the gate–harness–product contract in spec-gate-specs
description:
## Context (applies to every bead in epic gate-c7r)

`spec-gate` runs a product's executable specification from a separate spec repository and gates the product on the verdict. Invariant: the agent that changes the product may not touch the measurement (specs, drivers, ledger, judge pin, verdict). Two repositories:

- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate`: the product (the tool). Agents write here.
- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate-specs`: its spec repository. Agents only draft here, on a branch the operator merges (D-09, D-15). The agent that changes one repository in a task does not change the other in that task (D-11).

`spec-gate` is the first product judged by `spec-gate` (dog-fooding). Design and the 25 recorded decisions: `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate/docs/design.md`. Requirements: `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md` (ids minted by `~/code/tools/req`, never by hand). House rules: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (rule ids `cm-*`).

## What

The contract between the three parties to a judgment: the judging `spec-gate`, the spec repository's acceptance harness, and the product. It is written down in `spec-gate-specs` before either side is built. The spec-side and product-side beads are done by different agent sessions (D-11), so this document is the only thing they share. In black-box testing, the product's protocol is part of the spec.

It must fix:

- **The CLI surface of `spec-gate` v0.** The `judge` and `mint` commands, their arguments, and one distinct exit status each for pass, fail, void (could not judge: build failed, harness failed, spec checkout not on `main`) and refused (checksum mismatch).
- **The verdict document.** Machine-readable, naming the product commit, the spec commit, the judge release and checksum, the verdict, and each scenario's id, result and reason. The schema stays open for `sg-212` to extend later.
- **The ledger format.** Append-only, one entry per scenario per judgment, keyed by scenario `@id`, product commit and spec commit. It is diffable in git.
- **`spec-gate.toml`.**
  - `[sut]`: how the product is checked out and built.
  - `[judge]`: the pin.
  - `[gates] acceptance`: the harness is a command plus a results file, so a fixture spec repository can supply a trivial command that prints canned results instead of a Rust crate to build.
- **The harness results format** that `spec-gate` reads: per scenario, its tags, its result, and each step's result, including skipped and undefined. Prefer a format `cucumber` 0.23 already writes (its `output-json` feature) over a new one.

Then update `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate/docs/design.md` §6 and §7 to match. This is a docs-only edit in the product repository, and it is approved in the epic's operator-decision section.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The contract lives at one path in `spec-gate-specs`; every item above is specified, with an example document for each format.
- `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.toml` conforms to it.
- The design doc's §6 and §7 agree with it; neither restates what the other says.
- Delivered as a branch on `spec-gate-specs` for operator merge.

description:

Requirements: `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md` (ids minted by `~/code/tools/req`, never by hand). House rules: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (rule ids `cm-*`).

## What

The step definitions that make every in-scope scenario runnable through the `dsl` from `gate-c7r.2`. That covers `sg-dop.*`, `sg-397.*`, `sg-zf8.*`, `sg-i86.1` and the minting scenarios from `gate-c7r.1`. Each step is a single line that hands off to the DSL. `cucumber` runs with `fail_on_skipped`.

Every in-scope scenario must then be seen failing against the product scaffold commit (`gate-c7r.8`) for the reason its `Then` states. A harness error, a panic or a build failure is not a red: it means the scenario was never exercised.

This is done by an agent session that does not change `spec-gate` itself (D-11).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A deliberately undefined step makes the run fail, seen once and then removed. This proves `fail_on_skipped` is live.
- Against the scaffold commit, every in-scope scenario fails, and the per-scenario log shows the failing assertion. The bead's close note records the scaffold commit SHA and the list of scenario results.
- No scenario passes against the scaffold. A pass there would mean either the scenario or the stub is wrong; find which before going on.
- Delivered as a branch on `spec-gate-specs` for operator merge.

title: Red-first core: scenario lifecycle state machine and verdict function
description:
## Context (applies to every bead in epic gate-c7r)

`spec-gate` runs a product's executable specification from a separate spec repository and gates the product on the verdict. Invariant: the agent that changes the product may not touch the measurement (specs, drivers, ledger, judge pin, verdict). Two repositories:

- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate`: the product (the tool). Agents write here.
- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate-specs`: its spec repository. Agents only draft here, on a branch the operator merges (D-09, D-15). The agent that changes one repository in a task does not change the other in that task (D-11).

`spec-gate` is the first product judged by `spec-gate` (dog-fooding). Design and the 25 recorded decisions: `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate/docs/design.md`. Requirements: `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md` (ids minted by `~/code/tools/req`, never by hand). House rules: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (rule ids `cm-*`).

## What

The entities of red-first, as a pure functional core (cm-rlh), with no I/O.

- **The scenario lifecycle**, derived from a scenario's ledger entries in order. It is a state machine (cm-prk):
  - a sum type of states, each carrying only the data valid in it;
  - a pure transition function `(state, event) -> (state, effects)`;
  - an exhaustive match with no wildcard.
  
  States must distinguish at least: never seen; seen red (with the first red's product commit); counted; and rejected (its first result was a pass).
- **The verdict function.** It takes the scenario results of one judgment plus each scenario's lifecycle and returns pass, fail or void, with a reason per scenario. Zero scenarios fails (`sg-zf8.2`). Any skipped or undefined step fails, whatever the harness configuration said (`sg-zf8.1`). Any scenario that is not counted fails, named (`sg-397.2`, `.3`). A scenario without an `@id` fails, named (the criterion drafted in `gate-c7r.1`).

**Flagged in the epic, implement as stated:** "rejected" is permanent for that id. A later red does not rescue it, because `sg-397.1` requires the red before the first pass. Re-identification (remove the `@id` and re-mint) is the way out.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Property tests with `hegeltest` (cm-eqj) over generated ledger-entry sequences prove:
  - a scenario is counted if and only if a red precedes its first pass;
  - the transition function is total over every state and event pair;
  - the verdict is pass if and only if there is at least one scenario, every scenario is counted, and no step was skipped or undefined.
- The zero, one and many cases (cm-srn) are each an explicit example test: no entries; one red; red then green; green first; many scenarios with mixed results.
- `effect-audit` passes on the core crate.
- `cargo mutants` on the changed code, with survivors triaged through `mutation-triage` (cm-1qk). Every survivor is either killed or recorded as equivalent.

title: spec-gate workspace, house gates, and the not-implemented stub (red baseline)
description:
## Context (applies to every bead in epic gate-c7r)

`spec-gate` runs a product's executable specification from a separate spec repository and gates the product on the verdict. Invariant: the agent that changes the product may not touch the measurement (specs, drivers, ledger, judge pin, verdict). Two repositories:

- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate`: the product (the tool). Agents write here.
- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate-specs`: its spec repository. Agents only draft here, on a branch the operator merges (D-09, D-15). The agent that changes one repository in a task does not change the other in that task (D-11).

`spec-gate` is the first product judged by `spec-gate` (dog-fooding). Design and the 25 recorded decisions: `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate/docs/design.md`. Requirements: `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md` (ids minted by `~/code/tools/req`, never by hand). House rules: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (rule ids `cm-*`).

## What

The `spec-gate` Cargo workspace and a stub binary. The scaffold commit is the bootstrap's red baseline: the commit every in-scope scenario is first seen failing against.

- **Crates** follow `~/kbe/guides/rust-native-architecture-template.md`, with `hex-lint` roles from the first commit (domain, usecase, port-and-adapter, driven-adapter, driving-adapter, composition-root, as the code needs them).
- **Gates live from this commit:**
  - `hex-lint`;
  - `effect-audit` on domain crates;
  - `clippy::wildcard_enum_match_arm` at deny (cm-prk);
  - a no-comments gate that fails on any code comment except toolchain directives (cm-k7c);
  - `cargo nextest run`.
  
  One command runs them all.
- **The stub** exposes the CLI surface from `gate-c7r.5` and implements no behaviour. Every command exits with a not-implemented error that is distinct from every outcome in the contract. It must never emulate a verdict: a stub that always exits "fail" would turn every "the verdict is fail" scenario green before any red was seen.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `cargo build --release --locked` succeeds.

title: spec-gate mint
description:
## Context (applies to every bead in epic gate-c7r)

`spec-gate` runs a product's executable specification from a separate spec repository and gates the product on the verdict. Invariant: the agent that changes the product may not touch the measurement (specs, drivers, ledger, judge pin, verdict). Two repositories:

- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate`: the product (the tool). Agents write here.
- `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate-specs`: its spec repository. Agents only draft here, on a branch the operator merges (D-09, D-15). The agent that changes one repository in a task does not change the other in that task (D-11).

`spec-gate` is the first product judged by `spec-gate` (dog-fooding). Design and the 25 recorded decisions: `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate/docs/design.md`. Requirements: `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md` (ids minted by `~/code/tools/req`, never by hand). House rules: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (rule ids `cm-*`).

## What

The `spec-gate mint` use case, satisfying the minting criteria drafted in `gate-c7r.1`. It edits the feature files in place:
- adds an `@id` tag to every scenario that lacks one;
- never overwrites an existing id;
- never reuses an id;
- decides uniqueness against every feature file in the repository.

Ids are minted with the `hashid` crate at `~/code/tools/hashid`.

"Never re-mint" is an invariant to make unrepresentable rather than check (cm-jiu): the mint operation accepts only a scenario that carries no id.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Properties (`hegeltest`) prove:
  - running mint twice gives the same files as running it once;
  - no existing id changes;
  - every id across the repository is unique after mint.
- Unit tests against a fake feature-file port (cm-wah) cover zero, one and many untagged scenarios, and many files.
- One boundary integration test on real files in a temporary directory (cm-33k).
- `cargo mutants` on the changed code, with survivors triaged.
- The minting scenarios from `gate-c7r.1` pass when the harness runs against this commit.
